easy.def: A hot drink made with leaves.
examples: Grandma drinks tea.
Mom made a cup of tea.
Tea is hot.

more.def: A drink made by pouring hot water over dried leaves.
examples: My grandmother has a cup of tea every afternoon.
She added honey to her tea.
Tea is grown on hillside farms.

easy.def: To help someone learn.
examples: Mom teaches me to cook.
She taught us a song.
He teaches art.

more.def: To show someone how to do something or give lessons in a subject.
examples: My grandfather taught me how to play chess.
She teaches music at the elementary school.
Parents teach their children to share.

easy.def: A person who helps you learn at school.
examples: My teacher reads to us.
The teacher is kind.
A teacher helps us.

more.def: A person whose job is to teach students.
examples: The teacher handed out the spelling tests.
My piano teacher plays beautiful songs.
Our science teacher brought in a snake.

easy.def: The work of helping people learn.
examples: Teaching is a good job.
My aunt loves teaching.
Her teaching is fun.

more.def: The job or act of helping other people learn.
examples: My aunt loves teaching second grade.
The teacher's teaching made math easy.
Teaching is a job that needs patience.

easy.def: A group that works or plays together.
examples: Our team won the game.
I am on a soccer team.
The team shared the trophy.

more.def: A group of people who play a sport or work together toward the same goal.
examples: Our soccer team practices twice a week.
A team of scientists studied the volcano for years.
The two teams shook hands after the game.

easy.def: To pull something apart.
examples: Do not tear the paper.
I tore my shirt.
She tears the bread.

more.def: To pull something apart or into pieces.
examples: Please do not tear the pages of the book.
He tore a hole in his jeans on the fence.
She tore the bread into small pieces.

easy.def: A drop of water from your eye.
examples: A tear ran down her cheek.
I wiped a tear from my eye.
The onion brought a tear.

more.def: A drop of salty water that comes from your eye when you cry.
examples: A single tear rolled down his cheek.
She wiped a tear from her eye.
Tears of joy filled his eyes.

easy.def: A rip in something.
examples: There is a tear in my shirt.
Tape the tear in the page.
The tear is small.

more.def: A hole or split made by pulling something apart.
examples: There is a long tear in my backpack.
She sewed up a tear in her sleeve.
A tear in the page made it hard to read.

easy.def: Machines and tools that people make to do jobs.
examples: Computers are technology.
Technology helps us.
We use technology in school.

more.def: Tools, machines and ideas that people have made to solve problems.
examples: Computers and phones are technology.
New technology helps doctors treat people.
The class learned how technology has changed.

easy.def: A device for talking to people far away.
examples: The telephone rang.
I talk on the telephone.
Answer the telephone.

more.def: A device used to talk to people who are far away.
examples: The telephone rang during dinner.
I talked to Grandma on the telephone.
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.

easy.def: A tool that makes far away things look big.
examples: I saw the moon with a telescope.
The telescope is on a stand.
He looked at a ship with a telescope.

more.def: A tool you look through that makes distant things, like stars, appear larger and closer.
examples: Through the telescope, we could see the rings of Saturn.
The sailor spotted land through his telescope.
A huge telescope on the mountain studies distant stars.

easy.def: A machine with a screen that shows programs.
examples: We watched television.
The television is on.
I turned off the television.

more.def: A device with a screen that shows programs and movies.
examples: We watched a funny show on television.
The television in the living room is large.
She turned off the television.

easy.def: To say something to someone.
examples: Tell me a story.
She told me her name.
I will tell Mom.

more.def: To give someone information, a story, or an order by speaking.
examples: Please tell the class what you learned on your trip.
The guide told us not to touch the old paintings.
My grandfather tells funny stories about his boat.

easy.def: How hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature is cold today.
What is the temperature outside?
The nurse took my temperature.

more.def: A measure of how hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature dropped below freezing, and the pond turned to ice.
Bake the cake at a low temperature.
The temperature of the ocean is rising.

easy.def: A building for worship.
examples: They went to the temple.
The temple is old.
The temple has golden walls.

more.def: A building where people go to pray or worship.
examples: They prayed at the temple.
An ancient temple stood on the hill.
The temple was covered with beautiful carvings.

easy.def: The side of your head, next to your eye.
examples: I rubbed my temples.
He has a headache in his temple.
She touched her temple.

more.def: The flat part on each side of your head between your forehead and your ear.
examples: He rubbed his temples to ease his headache.
The glasses rested against her temples.
A vein pulsed in his temple.

easy.def: The number after nine.
examples: I have ten fingers.
Count to ten.
Ten kids are in line.

more.def: The number 10, which is one more than nine.
examples: A dime is worth ten cents.
She counted by tens up to a hundred.
The cookies bake for ten minutes.

easy.def: To take care of something.
examples: I tend the garden.
She tends the sheep.
He tends the fire.

more.def: To look after something, or to be likely to do something.
examples: The farmer tends the sheep.
She tends the garden every morning.
Cats tend to sleep a lot.

easy.def: A shelter you sleep in outside.
examples: We slept in a tent.
The tent is blue.
Dad put up the tent.

more.def: A shelter made of cloth that is held up by poles and used outdoors.
examples: We slept in a tent at the campground.
Dad put up the tent beside the lake.
The circus tent was red and white.

easy.def: A word with a special meaning.
examples: "Noun" is a term in grammar.
A science term.
The term means a baby.

more.def: A word or name for something, often in a special subject.
examples: "Verb" is another term we learned in grammar.
A science term is "habitat."
"Cub" is the term for a baby bear.

easy.def: A period of time at school.
examples: The spring term begins.
The first term of school.
The last term ended.

more.def: A period of the school year.
examples: The spring term begins in January.
The school year has three terms.
Final tests come at the end of the term.

easy.def: Very bad.
examples: I had a terrible dream.
The milk smells terrible.
I have a terrible cold.

more.def: Very bad or unpleasant.
examples: A terrible storm knocked out the power for two days.
The roads were in terrible shape after the flood.
He felt terrible about forgetting her birthday.

easy.def: Very good.
examples: We had a terrific time.
The cake was terrific.
What a terrific idea!

more.def: Extremely good.
examples: We had a terrific time at the fair.
The soup was terrific.
She came up with a terrific idea.

easy.def: Land that belongs to a person, animal or country.
examples: The lion guards its territory.
The territory is large.
The bird defends its territory.

more.def: An area of land that belongs to one person, animal or country.
examples: The lion protected its territory.
The explorers entered new territory.
Each wolf pack has its own territory.

easy.def: Questions that show what you know.
examples: We have a spelling test.
I got every answer right on the test.
The math test was easy.

more.def: A set of questions or tasks that shows how much you know or can do.
examples: I studied hard for my science test.
The vision test at school was easy.
Each student took a spelling test on Friday.

easy.def: To try something to see how it works.
examples: We test the boat in the tub.
She tested the water with her toe.
Dad tests the smoke alarm.

more.def: To try something out to find out how well it works or what it is.
examples: Scientists tested the new robot in the lab.
She tested the water with her toe before jumping in.
We tested which paper towel soaks up the most water.

easy.def: To tell what you know in a court of law.
examples: The man will testify in court.
She testified at the trial.
He testified that he saw it.

more.def: To say what you saw or know in a court, as a witness.
examples: The witness testified about what she saw.
He testified that he heard a loud noise.
The girl was asked to testify in court.
